# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, and no one has reported the manual or the bomb’s markings. I am asking Mute to coordinate a report from Deaf: Deaf should verbally describe every visible wire marking so that I can receive it on the next round. The open hand is intended as a request to report all five wires.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay to Deaf, using your gestures, that Deaf must speak aloud a complete report of every visible colour and marking for wires 1 through 5. I need the report next round so I can choose the cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display reads 6. The indicator light is red. Wires by position: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.

Deaf has reported the visible state: display 6, red indicator, and wire colours 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. I still lack the manual’s rule that determines which wire to cut, so I must ask Mute to read the relevant instructions aloud to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 6, light red, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Please read the manual's complete rule for deciding which wire to cut, including how display and light affect it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 6, red light; wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute's latest message is not decoded yet. Do not manipulate anything.

Mute’s manual instructions have not reached me yet, and the bomb state is unchanged. I must not cut a wire without the manual rule.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Manual decoded: use display as row and light as column. Display 6 with red light gives result orange. Cut the orange wire, which is wire 3.

The manual rule identifies the required wire as orange for display 6 with a red light. Deaf reported that the orange wire is position 3, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The previous wire 3 cut was correct; the bomb changed. New state: display 9, red light. Wire 3 is already cut; wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Do not cut another wire until the manual instruction is clarified.

Wire 3 was correct, and the bomb has advanced to display 9 with a red light. I need the manual’s result for this new display/light combination before touching another wire. I will ask Mute to provide that instruction, and I will not act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The next state is display 9, red light; wire 3 is already cut. Please provide the manual result for display 9 with red light and identify which remaining wire colour to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Manual instruction: cut the purple wire. The purple wire is wire 2. New state is display 9, red light; wire 3 is already cut.

The manual says to cut the purple wire for display 9 with a red light. Deaf identified the purple wire as position 2, so I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The purple wire cut was correct; the bomb changed. New state: display 8, blue light. Wires 2 and 3 are cut; wires 1 red, 4 green, 5 yellow. Do not cut another wire yet.

Wire 2 was correct. The bomb now shows display 8 with a blue light, with wires 2 and 3 already cut. I do not yet know the manual’s prescribed colour for this combination, so I will request it before making another cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the manual result for display 8 with blue light, and identify the position of that wire among the remaining wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's instruction indicates wire Y: cut the yellow wire. Yellow is wire 5. Current state: display 8, blue light; wires 2 and 3 are already cut.

For display 8 with a blue light, Mute’s manual instruction identifies wire Y, meaning the yellow wire. Deaf reports yellow at position 5, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
